transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I've been having terrible trouble sleeping for the past five days, and I feel constantly stressed and dazed. It all started so suddenly, and I really need some help to get through this.
In the week before your symptoms started, were you exposed to any event involving actual or threatened death, serious injury, or violence?
Honestly, my mind has been feeling so foggy and overwhelmed lately. I'm not really sure, and I can't clearly recall or explain any specific event right now.
Has anything difficult or out of the ordinary happened in your life in the past month, even if it didn’t feel traumatic at the time?

I can't recall any specific event, but I have been feeling extremely overwhelmed and stressed for the past five days. It feels like everything is just a blur right now and I'm struggling to get through each day.
Did your symptoms start within one month of a stressful life event, and have they lasted for less than one month so far?
Yes, my symptoms started right after a very stressful event. It has only been five days so far that I've been feeling this way.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Acute Stress Disorder", "Adjustment Disorder"], but based on this conversation, Adjustment Disorder is less likely because the patient's symptoms (trouble sleeping, feeling dazed, and significant stress) began immediately after a stressful event and are within the first month, which aligns more specifically with Acute Stress Disorder. The sudden onset, presence of dissociative symptoms (feeling dazed, foggy mind), and time frame (five days) following a stressor strongly support Acute Stress Disorder. Adjustment Disorder typically involves emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor but does not include prominent dissociative features or acute stress reactions of this intensity. Therefore, the current candidate is narrowed to Acute Stress Disorder.
